A CT scan shows evidence of a fistula and strictures located in the last 30 cm of her ileum. A resection of the affected portion of the bowel is scheduled. What changes in bile metabolism are expected in this patient post-procedure?

                    ### Options

opb. Synthesis of cholesterol in the liver will decrease

This leads to decreased enterohepatic circulation of bile acids, prompting the liver to increase bile acid synthesis from cholesterol, thereby altering the balance of bile components. This aligns with option 'opc'. The synthesis of cholesterol in the liver may increase to compensate for the increased conversion to bile acids, contradicting option 'opb'. The absorption of 7⍺-dehydroxylated bile acids, which are secondary bile acids reabsorbed in the ileum, will decrease, supporting option 'ope'. The resection does not directly affect enteric bacteria in the small intestine, making option 'opd' less relevant. The absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, including vitamin K, is likely impaired due to decreased bile acid availability, contradicting option 'opa'. The retrieved evidence path regarding vitamin K and fat-soluble vitamins supports the consensus that vitamin K absorption may be impaired post-resection.
